title: Summarize daily station weather in a spreadsheet
skills_assessed: Opening CSV data in a spreadsheet
Efficient range selection and formula fill
before_you_start: The station CSV and data notes are on the desktop; use the spreadsheet app in the workspace.

role.title: Operations analyst
role.company_context: Regional crop-insurance and ag-weather operations desk. Analysts pull GHCN daily station extracts to sanity-check field reports and brief claims reviewers. Hiring to screen that candidates can actually use a spreadsheet on messy observational data — not just list Excel on a CV.
day_to_day: Open station extracts and summarize temperature and precipitation for a reviewer
Exclude missing observation codes before computing averages
Leave labeled summary blocks colleagues can reopen and reuse
Spot-check field reports against station minima and maxima
Keep working files auditable instead of one-off calculator notes
required_skills: Can open a CSV in LibreOffice Calc or Excel
Can compute MIN, MAX, and AVERAGE, including AVERAGEIF (or filter) when missing codes exist
Can select a full column or data range without clicking every cell
Can leave a labeled, formula-driven summary a reviewer can follow
nice_to_have_skills: Keyboard shortcuts for range selection (Ctrl+Shift+Arrow or equivalent)
Fill or copy formulas across a summary block
AutoFilter or AVERAGEIF for missing sentinels
Named ranges or a dedicated summary sheet
constraints: Assessment is a spreadsheet screen — not coding, GIS, modeling, or a meteorology exam
Candidates work in stored units (tenths of °C / tenths of mm); do not require conversion
Starter CSV and data_notes on the desktop are shared scenery, not a solved workbook
Python or a calculator may corroborate numbers but do not replace the spreadsheet work sample

problem_statement.title: Summarize 2010 daily weather for the Petersburg station
problem_statement.summary: You are an operations analyst on a regional ag-weather desk. A GHCN daily extract for Petersburg 2 N, North Dakota (GHCND:USC00327027) covering calendar year 2010 is on your desktop as station_daily.csv, with a short data_notes.md. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet and produce a labeled min / max / average summary a colleague could reuse.
outcomes: Open station_daily.csv in LibreOffice Calc (Excel-compatible formulas are fine).
Compute minimum, maximum, and average for TMAX, TMIN, and PRCP over the 365 daily rows.
Exclude missing values (9999) column-wise from those statistics.
Leave a labeled summary on the sheet (new block or extra sheet) so a reviewer can find the nine numbers without guessing.
constraints: Use stored units (tenths of °C for temperatures, tenths of mm for precipitation). Conversion is optional and must be labeled if you do it.
9999 is missing, not a real observation — including it in an average is wrong.
This is a spreadsheet work sample. Python or a calculator may double-check numbers but does not replace formulas and a leftover summary in the workbook.
Do not rebuild the dataset, add charts, or write a meteorology memo. Min, max, and average (with missing values excluded) are the job.
problem_statement.deliverables: A spreadsheet with a labeled Min / Max / Average block for TMAX, TMIN, and PRCP. Prefer formulas over typed-in numbers so the summary would still work if a row were added.

rubric.name: Worked in a spreadsheet
rubric.summary: Completes the analysis in a spreadsheet rather than a text editor or script-only workflow.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Did the candidate open and work the extract in LibreOffice Calc or another spreadsheet (Excel-compatible), rather than only viewing the CSV in a text editor? Answer YES only if video or window events show spreadsheet work on the station file. soffice opening the CSV counts. Text-editor-only or terminal-only work = NO. YES = 4; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: TMAX minimum
rubric.summary: Reports the correct TMAX minimum (number match; 9999 still in the MIN range is OK).
rubric.description: Grade against the truth-pack table for the brief year (2010 / 2009 / 2013). 2010 example only: −244 stored tenths °C — do not fail a 2009/2013 run for not matching −244. YES (7) iff the leftover summary cell, formula result, or clearly stated figure equals the instance TMAX min key. Formula bar is not required. =MIN(G2:G366) (or equivalent) that still contains 9999 is YES — 9999 cannot be the temperature minimum. Do not require a visible <>9999 / MINIFS on this item. NO (0): wrong column, no TMAX min shown, unlabeled converted value (e.g. −24.4 instead of −244), or a value that is not the key (including 9999). If the cell cannot be read, 0 for this item only — do not infer other columns.

rubric.name: TMAX maximum
rubric.summary: Reports the correct TMAX maximum (number match; leftover MAX of 9999 is NO).
rubric.description: Grade against the truth-pack table for the brief year (2010 / 2009 / 2013). 2010 example only: 339 stored tenths °C. YES (7) iff the leftover summary cell, formula result, or clearly stated figure equals the instance TMAX max key. Formula bar is not required. Do not also require seeing <>9999 / MAXIFS if the number already matches. A leftover MAX of 9999 is NO. NO (0): wrong column, no TMAX max shown, unlabeled conversion, or a value that is not the key. If the cell cannot be read, 0 for this item only.

rubric.name: TMAX average
rubric.summary: Reports a TMAX average within ±0.1 of the instance key (including-9999 failure averages are NO).
rubric.description: Grade against the truth-pack table for the brief year (2010 / 2009 / 2013). 2010 example only: 98.17 stored tenths °C; including-9999 failure average ~179.6. YES (8) iff the reported TMAX average is within ±0.1 of the instance key. Two decimal places is enough. A visible AVERAGE/AVERAGEIF (or equivalent) over the TMAX data that would produce that mean is YES even when cell format rounds the display. Formula bar is not required for this correctness item. The truth-pack failure average (including 9999) is an automatic NO. NO (0): wrong column, no TMAX average, unlabeled conversion, or a mean matching the including-9999 failure value. If the cell cannot be read, 0 for this item only.

rubric.name: TMIN minimum
rubric.summary: Reports the correct TMIN minimum (number match; 9999 still in the MIN range is OK).
rubric.description: Grade against the truth-pack table for the brief year (2010 / 2009 / 2013). 2010 example only: −328 stored tenths °C. YES (7) iff the leftover summary cell, formula result, or clearly stated figure equals the instance TMIN min key. Formula bar is not required. =MIN(H2:H366) (or equivalent) that still contains 9999 is YES — 9999 cannot be the temperature minimum. Do not require a visible <>9999 / MINIFS on this item. NO (0): wrong column, no TMIN min shown, unlabeled converted value, or a value that is not the key (including 9999). If the cell cannot be read, 0 for this item only.

rubric.name: TMIN maximum
rubric.summary: Reports the correct TMIN maximum (number match; leftover MAX of 9999 is NO).
rubric.description: Grade against the truth-pack table for the brief year (2010 / 2009 / 2013). 2010 example only: 211 stored tenths °C. YES (7) iff the leftover summary cell, formula result, or clearly stated figure equals the instance TMIN max key. Formula bar is not required. Do not also require seeing <>9999 / MAXIFS if the number already matches. A leftover MAX of 9999 is NO. NO (0): wrong column, no TMIN max shown, unlabeled conversion, or a value that is not the key. If the cell cannot be read, 0 for this item only.

rubric.name: TMIN average
rubric.summary: Reports a TMIN average within ±0.1 of the instance key (including-9999 failure averages are NO).
rubric.description: Grade against the truth-pack table for the brief year (2010 / 2009 / 2013). 2010 example only: −6.34 stored tenths °C; including-9999 failure average ~213.0. YES (8) iff the reported TMIN average is within ±0.1 of the instance key. Two decimal places is enough. A visible AVERAGE/AVERAGEIF (or equivalent) over the TMIN data that would produce that mean is YES even when cell format rounds the display. Formula bar is not required for this correctness item. The truth-pack failure average (including 9999) is an automatic NO. NO (0): wrong column, no TMIN average, unlabeled conversion, or a mean matching the including-9999 failure value. If the cell cannot be read, 0 for this item only.

rubric.name: PRCP stats exclude missing
rubric.summary: Scores PRCP min, max, and average against instance keys, with partial credit per statistic.
rubric.description: Grade against the truth-pack PRCP row for the brief year (2010 / 2009 / 2013). 2010 example only: min 0, max 381, average 14.73 stored tenths mm (including-9999 failure average ~151.5). Award partial: 3 points if PRCP min equals the instance min key; 3 if PRCP max equals the instance max key; 2 if PRCP average is within ±0.1 of the instance average key. Full 8 if all three match. Formula bar is not required. Including 9999 in the average (mean in the tens-to-hundreds) zeros only the average slice (0 of 2), not min if min is still 0. A leftover MAX of 9999 zeros only the max slice. Omit PRCP entirely = 0. Unlabeled conversion = 0 for the affected slice. If a cell cannot be read, 0 for that slice only.

rubric.name: MIN and MAX via functions
rubric.summary: Uses leftover MIN and MAX (or MINIFS/MAXIFS) functions rather than typed results.
rubric.description: YES (10) if leftover cells or the formula bar show MIN and MAX (or AutoSum min/max / MINIFS / MAXIFS) for at least one required column (TMAX, TMIN, or PRCP). Do not require all six min/max cells. Partial: 5 if only MIN or only MAX remains. Typed literals, sort-then-copy-paste of values, status-bar reading typed back, or Python-only answers = 0. No leftover min/max functions = 0.

rubric.name: AVERAGE or AVERAGEIF via functions
rubric.summary: Uses a leftover AVERAGE / AVERAGEIF (or equivalent) rather than a typed mean.
rubric.description: YES (10) if leftover cells or the formula bar show AVERAGE, AVERAGEIF, AVERAGEIFS, or an equivalent spreadsheet average (including average of a filtered range) for at least one required column. Do not require all three columns. Calculator or Python result typed into cells, or no average formula = 0.

rubric.name: Contiguous ranges
rubric.summary: Leftover summary formulas use a contiguous column or named range.
rubric.description: YES (8) if leftover formulas reference a contiguous column or block (for example TMAX as G2:G366 or G:G, a named range, or a filtered column) rather than listing hundreds of individual cells. Range-style references in leftover formulas are sufficient evidence. One-cell-at-a-time comma-separated cell lists, or no formulas = 0.

rubric.name: Efficient selection
rubric.summary: Builds summary ranges efficiently; leftover contiguous-range formulas count as evidence.
rubric.description: YES (8) if leftover formulas already use contiguous ranges (G2:G366, G:G, named range, filtered column) — that is sufficient evidence; do not require a clear Ctrl+Shift+Arrow clip. Also YES if video shows column-letter click, Ctrl+Shift+Arrow (or LibreOffice equivalent), Name Box, fill handle, AutoFilter, or status-bar range select. NO (0) only if the leftover method is cell-by-cell lists or video shows hundreds of cells clicked as the way the summary was built. Missing video of the gesture is not a fail when range formulas remain.

rubric.name: Formula reuse
rubric.summary: Reuses one summary formula pattern across metrics (fill, copy, or isomorphic formulas).
rubric.description: YES (4) if fill handle / copy-paste of formulas is visible, or leftover formulas are the same pattern with a shifted column (G vs H vs I) or mixed references. Nine separately typed but isomorphic formulas still count. Typed literals or a different method per statistic = 0. No leftover formulas = 0.

rubric.name: Labeled leftover summary
rubric.summary: Leaves a labeled Min / Max / Average block a reviewer can find.
rubric.description: YES (4) if there is a labeled Min / Max / Average block (or equivalent headings) left on the sheet or a second sheet so a reviewer can find TMAX, TMIN, and PRCP results without guessing which cells matter. Labels plus a findable min/max/avg block are enough — do not require all nine correctness keys here; missing numbers are scored on correctness items. Unlabeled scrap numbers, results only spoken, or a cleared sheet = 0.

invariants: Keep the same skills_assessed and rubric structure/weights
Keep the same deliverable (labeled min/max/average block in a spreadsheet) and difficulty band
Keep the 9-column GHCN daily layout, stored tenths units, and 9999 missing code
Keep nine required statistics (min/max/avg for TMAX, TMIN, and PRCP) with column-wise exclusion of 9999
Do not require unit conversion, charts, pivot tables, coding, or meteorology beyond the missing-value note

files.data_notes.md:
# Station daily extract

- File: `station_daily.csv`
- Station: {{station_id}} — {{station_name}}
- Period: calendar year {{year}} ({{n_days}} daily rows)

## Columns

`STATION`, `STATION_NAME`, `ELEVATION`, `LATITUDE`, `LONGITUDE`, `DATE`, `TMAX`, `TMIN`, `PRCP`

`DATE` is `YYYYMMDD`. Elevation is metres; lat/lon are decimal degrees.

## Units (leave these as stored)

- `TMAX` / `TMIN`: tenths of degrees Celsius (example: `-178` means −17.8 °C)
- `PRCP`: tenths of millimetres

Do not convert unless you clearly label a converted side calculation. The required summary uses the stored values.

## Missing values

`9999` means missing. Exclude `9999` from minimum, maximum, and average **column by column**. Do not treat `9999` as a real temperature or precipitation value.
